cohort: The study included 135,379 adult patients (aged ≥18 years) admitted between January 1, 2013, and September 30, 2015, who underwent hospital-based surgical or endoscopic procedures and received opioids.
finding: Opioid-related adverse drug events (ORADEs) were common among surgical patients and were significantly associated with worse clinical outcomes (increased inpatient mortality, discharge to another care facility, prolonged length of stay, higher 30-day readmission) and increased cost of hospitalization.
